mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following low FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in at least 60% of the 20-day periods after UNRATE drops below 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GDP and housing starts indicate strong economic demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day periods following rising GDPC1 and HOUST, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth indicates increased supply and economic activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in at least 70% of the 60-day periods after INDPRO growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following PAYEMS growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail sales signals strong consumer demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in at least 60% of the 20-day periods after RSAFS increases by 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rates combined with high unemployment rates may indicate economic stress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 60-day periods when FEDFUNDS is low and UNRATE is high, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing GDP growth during a late-cycle expansion may signal an upcoming economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth slows by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show negative returns in at least 50% of the 60-day periods after GDPC1 growth slows, the hypothesis is rejected.
